characters.name: In General
characters.description: Academic Athlete: Two geniuses with their own athleticism. The Ace: There's almost nothing Phineas and Ferb can't do. Adorably Precocious Child: In the sense that they are the most worldly-wise of the kid characters in the show. Ambiguously Absent Parent: No canon mention is ever made of Phineas' biological father or Ferb's biological mother, though creators Dan Povenmire and Swampy Marsh have officially stated that Phineas's fatheris not Heinz Doofenshmirtz(or, for that matter,Bill Cipher, despite anything you might have heard inThe Book of Bill).(There is a mention in the non-canon Star Wars special when long lost' Candace asked Phineas if their parents divorced. Phineas says it's a funny story, and then he starts to tell it,only to be interrupted by the Death Star exploding). Annoying Younger Sibling: Candace sees Phineas and Ferb as this due to their childish naivety, though they are a rare example where they don't do it on purpose.

characters.name: Isabella Garcia-Shapiro
characters.description: A girl who lives across the way from Phineas and Ferb and is a good friend of theirs. Isabella is a multi-talented member of theFireside Girlswithquite a number of accomplishment patchesto her name. She has a not-so-secret crush on Phineas, and likes to pop in once an episode to ask Phineas "What'cha doin'?" and offer to help. The Ace: She has an exceptionally versatile set of skills and is extremely bright and athletic. She uses these abilities to earn Fireside Girl patches — a girl scout group which presents challenges varying from extremely difficult to outright ridiculous. "Act Your Age" reveals that she becomes a resident assistant by the time she starts her first year of college and has joined numerous diverse student organizations. Action Girl: Not shown that often, but comes out in spades when it does. She has defeated Mitch, trashed countless Norm Bots during theFinal BattleinAcross the 2nd Dimension, and saved all of Danville from being trapped in the form of pharmacist zombies. Adaptational Personality Change: InPhineas and Ferb: Star Wars, Isabella, instead of being a cheerfulNice GirlandGirly Girl with a Tomboy Streak, is now aJerk with a Heart of Goldbadass pilot to make her act more likeHan Solo, with the only thing she shares with any version of Isabella is that she develops romantic feelings for Phineas. Even her catchphrase, "What'cha doin'?", is delivered in a far more irritated manner as opposed to the cheerful tone she uses in canon. Arc Symbol: Like how Phineas is represented by triangles and Ferb by rectangles, Isabella is represented by semicircles, sharing this shape with Candace. This is seen in the background of the credits version of "Tip of the Day", and how Isabella's head is shaped like a semicircle that has the flat side on top.

characters.name: Baljeet Tjinder
characters.description: A shrimpyBollywood Nerdwho's more than a little obsessed with order and studying. He's a friend of Phineas and Ferb who occasionally joins in on their daily activity, or even seeks out their advice. Occasionally, they also seek out his, usually when it comes to things like checking their math. Absurd Phobia: He considers a failed math test to be the scariest thing known to man. He also fears contractions. Adorably Precocious Child: He's quite mature and serious about his schoolwork. All There in the Script: His surname, which different sources had given as either Patel, Rai, or Raj. It was finally confirmed to be Tjinder on Swampy Marsh'sTwitterin 2012, and then solidified in "It's No Picnic" Arc Symbol: Circles, as seen in the credits of "Tip of the Day".

characters.name: Buford Van Stomm
characters.description: While introduced as the dim-witted, thuggish local bully, Buford has some surprisingHidden Depths, and he eventually becomes a member of Phineas and Ferb's circle of friends. He still exercises a slightly twisted sense of humor, and likes to hang out with Baljeet largely (but not entirely) so he has an easy target for bullying handy. Affectionate Nickname: He often calls Phineas "Dinnerbell", in reference to his triangular-shaped head. It was first used as a bullying tactic, but later evolved into this. All Drummers Are Animals: Whenever the gang forms a band for a musical number, he plays the drums. Although one exception is "Come Home Perry", where Baljeet was the drummer instead (he usually is seen playing keyboards) and Buford instead plays the cowbell. Amazon Chaser: He expresses attraction to girls who act "tough" in some way (but, interestingly, never towards Isabella, despite her having such tendencies up to and including beating him at sports). Ambiguously Bi: Has expressed crushes on girls, specifically Candace, but his relationship with Baljeet is enough to raise eyebrows, and in multiple Season 5 episodes he openly hits on Jeremy.

characters.name: Candace Flynn
characters.description: Phineas and Ferb's high-strung, neurotic, obsessive, and paranoid older sister. Like most teenage girls, she's obsessed with clothes-shopping, pop music, chatting on the phone, hanging with her friends, and boys (in particular her crush, Jeremy Johnson). Unlike most teenage girls, she's also obsessed with "busting" her brothers for their outlandish schemes. Candace tries constantly to expose their projects to their mom, but every time she comes home, the projects are gone and Candace is left stunned, sometimes leading Linda to forcibly take Candace away or send her to her room, or on some occasions, Candace herself gets punished instead. Often, she sometimes approves of the projects and still loves her brothers one and the same. Absurd Phobia: For reasons unknown, she fears the number seven, even stranger considering her own name has seven letters. She is alsoarachnophobic, as revealed in "Save Summer", as well as acrophobic. Granted the latter two are very common phobias Accidental Athlete: Happens to Candace fairly often showing a remarkable athletic prowess of the girl. A good example in "Phineas' Birthday Clip-o-Rama!" where she performs impressive stunts to preserve the DVD that contains all the proof she will ever need of P&F's projects. We even have a kid asking her for an autograph after all of that! Achilles' Heel: In the 2009Nintendo DSgame, one of the items used to distract Candace from watching the brothers is the strawberry shortcake (which is unusual, considering herTrademark Favorite Foodis grilled cheese). Acquired Situational Narcissism: In "We Call It Maze", she lets the praise of "Little Spark" Melissa over her earning fifty Fireside Girl patches in a day go to her head, and she starts talking down to Isabella and thinking she knows how to do everything. After her decisions end up getting the three of them in trouble, Candace isforced to admitshe only earned the patches through Phineas, Ferb and Isabella's help.

characters.name: Linda Flynn-Fletcher and Lawrence Fletcher
characters.description: Phineas, Ferb and Candace's parents. Linda is an ordinary suburban mom who somehow remains oblivious to the crazy things Phineas and Ferb do, despite Candace's futile efforts to show her. Lawrence is an eccentric, slightly geeky antiques dealer who sometimes joins in on Phineas and Ferb's hijinks. Abusive Parents: Downplayed and slightly justified for the both of them. They love their kids, but can come off as negligent or unreasonable, usually because they don't know the whole situation.Lawrence on the face of it is genuinely accepting of his boys creative projects and such, but he is also absurdly complacent and inattentive to the point that he's along for the ride even when things get more wild and dangerous, or the boys work on something they shouldn't (like Linda's car), it also causes him to be occasionally confused when people act negatively.Linda leans further into this trope as an emotional variation. For the most part, she's a very pleasant person and a good mother to her children whom respect her. However, whenever Candace begins going on about the boys, Linda tends to drop pleasantries and very quickly not try very hard, usually rolling her eyes, insulting Candace or in the worst case scenerios, ignoring Candace outright. To say this cycle of being disbelieved and insulted by Linda has damaged Candace's psyche to a degree would be anUnderstatement, and it leads to further erratic behavior and getting herself hurt trying to prove things to Linda.Not helping are scenarios where Lindadoesactually catch Phineas and Ferb. When that that happens, she consistently flips her lid to the point and leans too far theopposite way, tending to lead parental movements which causedictatorships to be set up or have kids re-educated into creatively sterile drones.Tellingly these situations tend to be undone to preservetheformula.An episode where the casttravel to the future (where Phineas and Ferbs inventions have become commonplace and made them famous). Adult!Candace tec

characters.name: Stacy Hirano
characters.description: Candace's best friend since childhood. Stacy is remarkably more laid-back and unfocused than Candace, and usually tries (with little or no success) to convince her to lighten up over busting Phineas and Ferb, trying to impress Jeremy, or whatever else Candace is worrying about.She also knows about Perry's secret identity, and later becomes an agent for O.W.C.A. Action Girl: When the situation calls for it. She helps fight off the Norm Bot invasion inAcross the 2nd Dimension. "Agent T (For Teen)" reveals that she knows taekwondo, which she uses whilerescuing Perry from L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N. Parodied in "Phineas and Ferb-Busters!", when Candace makes her and Jenny go through some physically taxing exercises so they can assist her in busting Phineas and Ferb. All Women Love Shoes: Stacy seems to love shoes enough to make a gelatin mold of some pumps. Ascended Extra: In the first season, she appeared infrequently, if at all (she was originally just an unheard voice on the other end of Candace's cell phone conversations). From the second season onward, it's relatively rare to see an episode where she doesn't appear, even if it's only for a scene or two, and she started playing more of a role in the plot of some episodes ("Put That Putter Away", "Elementary, My Dear Stacy", "Phineas and Ferb-Busters!", "The Lemonade Stand"). In contrast to Jeremy beingDemoted to Extrain Season 5, Stacy has gained even more prominence during the revival, becoming much more involved in the plots and gaining a newA Day in the Limelightepisode. Asian Airhead: Downplayed. She has occasionalCloudcuckoolandertendencies and is sometimes shown to lack basic knowledge about geography, but Candace's own personal manias often make Stacy the more level-headed one by comparison. And then there are moments of being smarter than Candace such as Candace saying boys are like the Egyptian drawings no one understands, only for Stacy to give a brief history on how the hieroglyphics were figured out, which Cand

characters.name: Jeremy Johnson
characters.description: A nice and easy-going local boy who is the object of Candace's affections. He works at the local fast-food outlet, Mr. Slushy Burger, and plays in a band, "Jeremy and the Incidentals". Later episodes expand on his originally flat characterization, giving him a bit of a snarky side when Candace is freaking out over something or another. Alliterative Name:JeremyJohnson. Birthday Episode: "Cheers for Fears". Boy Next Door: To Candace, in a rare male example. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: Gender-inverted with him and Candace. He's the laid-back and sweet-natured Gentle Boy to Candace's aggressive and neurotic Brooding Girl.

characters.name: Perry the Platypus (Agent P)
characters.description: Phineas and Ferb's faithful pet. He's a platypus, andthey don't do much... or so the boys think. Secretly, he's actually a highly skilled secret agent for O.W.C.A. (the Organization Without a Cool Acronym), and he usually slips awayOnce per Episodeto deal with whatever crazy scheme his arch nemesis, Dr. Doofenshmirtz, has cooked up. For tropes pertaining to his appearances inMilo Murphy's Law, seehere. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal:"Besides his hat, he wears no clothes" The Ace: He's one of the best agents at O.W.C.A.. Action Pet: A badass secret agent in an agency where virtually all of the field agents areaction pets, and have aFedora of Asskickingas their uniform.

characters.name: Vanessa Doofenshmirtz
characters.description: Dr. Doofenshmirtz's teenage daughter. When she's not being embarrassed by her father's bungling attempts at being evil, she's being embarrassed by his attempts at doting on her. Despite all that, she does love him. Given that her father is, legally, an ocelot, she would (possibly) legally be identified as technicallyhalf-ocelot, despite being biologically fully human. Aborted Arc: "I Scream, You Scream" and "Hail Doofania!" set up a subplot in which she attempted to prove to her mother that her father was evil, but this was dropped in the second season so as not to make her "Goth Candace". Action Girl: Just watch "Vanessassary Roughness" where it shows what she's capable of when motivated. Her"I Am" Song"I'm Me"from that episode showcases her in action. Affectionate Nickname: She is sometimes called just "Nessa" for short.

characters.name: Major Francis Monogram
characters.description: Perry's immediate superior. It's to him that Perry reports each episode to get a briefing on whatever Dr. Doofenshmirtz is up to. Despite his usually stiff and serious demeanor, it's been shown that he's actually a bit scatterbrained, with his briefings being vague or otherwise unhelpful. Alliterative Name: Only when referred to in his official capacity: Major Monogram. As You Know: Reminds Perry (and the audience) of O.W.C.A. policies when they become plot-relevant. Ascended Extra: He was originally meant to be nothing more than atalking head on a screenwho sent Perry on his missions, but he soon gained an unpaid intern, was eventually revealed to have a son, and had significant roles in multiple episodes (notably "Where's Perry?" and "Save Summer"). Beware the Silly Ones: He may act goofy much of the time, but he can also more than hold his own in a fight.

characters.name: Carl Karl
characters.description: Major Monogram's assistant, a nerdy college intern working for O.W.C.A. who occasionally banters back and forth with Monogram while Perry the Platypus is being sent out on a mission. Action Survivor: In "Save Summer", he helps Perry and Monty sneak into the headquarters of L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N. but is noticeably (and understandably) less involved in the action than they are. Alliterative Name: Sort of.CarlKarl. Awesomeness by Analysis:Which makes him quite a competent threat after being turned evil. He was able to infer Perry's whereabouts correctly by identifying an obscure flower he saw in the background while video-calling Perry. Butt-Monkey: In the sense that he's frequently berated and ignored, often unfairly.

characters.name: Phineas Flynn
characters.description: A cheerful boy who's always coming up with wild ideas of what to do over summer vacation, from building a humongous rollercoaster to traveling into outer space to breeding giant mutant sea-monkeys. Even ordinary activities such as running a lemonade stand or making ice-cream sundaes get taken up to eleven when Phineas gets involved. 10-Minute Retirement: When he is brutally brainwashed in "Phineas and Ferb Get Busted!" and when he is unable to come up with a way to escape the island in "Summer Belongs to You!". Allergic to Routine: His projects for the summer are a result of this. Note that all his projects and games tend to be a variant ofCalvinball. Alliterative Name:PhineasnotePronounced identically to an FFlynn. All-Loving Hero: Even to the most hostile of individuals, Phineas exhibits nothing but kindness.Most of the time.

characters.name: Ferbs "Ferb" Fletcher
characters.description: Phineas' stepbrother and best friend. A quiet and stoic boy who usually says no more than one or two lines per episode. He's also a mechanical genius who gladly helps his brother assemble whatever contrived contraption they need for their latest scheme. The Ace: Though he and Phineas fill this role together, Ferb is shown to be even more capable than his stepbrother. He can teleport, speaks several languages including Martian, and is able to build anything the plot requires. Agent Mulder: He believes in curses and is reluctant to try to fight them. He blocked his eyes when he thought Candace was a gorgon, and he backed away when Candace thought she was a vampire. Alliterative Name:FerbFletcher. Animal-Themed Superbeing: As the Beak.

characters.name: #-D
characters.description: 10-Minute Retirement:The Season 4 finalehas him give up his supervillain career after realizing how unfulfilling it was andthat he's not as bad a person as he sold himself to be. Season 5 has him relapsing back into villainy as early as the first 5 minutes. Absurd Phobia: He has many fears, including heights, bats, shellfish, and sentient vending machines taking over the world. He was able to get over his fears of heights, bats, and vending machines, but not with shellfish. Abusive Parents: Not him, he's a good (if embarrassing) father to Vanessa, but his parents were a major contributor to hisHilariously Abusive Childhood. His mother immediately re-gifted his toy teddy bear present to Roger, and when the Doofenshmirtzes' lawn gnomes were repossessed, his father had him act as a replacement lawn gnome for hours on end. Accidental Misnaming: In "Ain't No Kiddie Ride". It's made funnier by the fact that everyone knows and loves his brother with the same exact last name. Achilles' Heel: He will never build anything without aSelf-Destruct Mechanism. When his plans fail, a good chunk of the time it is for this reason. According to Doof himself, it's becausehe needs an easy way out in the event of his dangerous -inators getting out of his control, which in some episodes is exactly what happens.

characters.name: Troop  46231 in General
characters.description: A group of Isabella's friends from the local Fireside Girls troop. Whenever she helps out with one of Phineas and Ferb's schemes, they often end up getting pulled into the antics too. Action Girls: They are very mechanically skilled and capable of some crazy stunts. Some of their achievement patches require very physically demanding activities. Badass Adorable: The Fireside Girls can earn patches for wrestlingalligatorsandmoving mountains. Their theme song even includes the lyrics, "We stand cute, small, and strong." Butt-Monkey:Ginger in "Isabella and the Temple of Sap", being teased whenever she expresses attraction to Baljeet.Adyson gets hit hard with it in "The Great Indoors," undergoing several accidents. Ginger in "Isabella and the Temple of Sap", being teased whenever she expresses attraction to Baljeet.

characters.name: Gretchen
characters.description: Black Bead Eyes: Gretchen has really dark blue dots for eyes to emphasize her glasses, and she seems to be the only member of the cast to have these. Notably, her stone-age counterpart has normal eyes instead. Boyish Short Hair: Gretchen's hair is the shortest of the Fireside Girls, highlighting her intelligence. Brainy Brunette: She once got a "Saying a Word No One Else in the Room Knows" patch for saying "Sesquipedalian". Child Prodigy: While all the Fireside Girls are this to some extent, this is most evident with Gretchen. Expy:Gretchen has reddish-brown hair, wears glasses, is around nine-ish, speaks inSesquipedalian Loquaciousness... just likeanotherGretchen.Short. Short hair. Small eyes. Glasses.Pheebs, is that you?

characters.name: Ginger Hirano
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Ginger has had noticeably more focus than the others in Season 4, probably because her relationships with Stacy and Baljeet provide additional dynamics beyond simply being backup support for the title characters. Big Sister Worship: Ginger is quite an overachiever, but she won all those trophies so she could impress Stacy. Deadpan Snarker: In "Bee Day" and "It's No Picnic," she snarks at Isabella's crush on Phineas, prompting Isabella to reprimand her with a "Stand down, Fireside Girl" both times. There's also this exchange in "Bee Story":Adyson:I know! We can get stung by radioactive bees and gain bee-themed superpowers!Holly:Um...we don't have access to radioactive bees.Ginger:Yeah.That'swhat's wrong with that plan. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: A downplayed trope, with Stacy being the lazy, underachieving teenager to Ginger's trophy-winning, mountain-moving Fireside Girl. Green-Eyed Monster: "Act Your Age" shows that when Ginger started dating Baljeet she developed a long-standing jealousy of his childhood friend Mishti given Adyson's long-suffering admonition to "let it go" when Ginger mumbled angrily about Mishti.

characters.name: Adyson Sweetwater
characters.description: Cheated Angle: When she moves her head to the side, her bangs swoop to the other side. Cloudcuckoolander: She says aloud that if she was stung by radioactive bees, she could get superpowers. Deadpan Snarker: "Isabella and the Temple of Sap" reveals that she has a sarcastic side.Isabella:So, did you guys decide what patch to get today? 'Cause I have a suggestion!Adyson:Lemme guess, Let's Help Phineas and Ferb Patch?Isabella:It's called the "Help Thy Neighbor" patch, Adyson. Don't make up patch names. Girly Girl: Adyson appears to be the most feminine of the Fireside Girls in "Act Your Age" given herblue dress, herLovable Alpha Bitchpersonality, her being the only one in the group to wear lipstick, and her being the most enthusiastic about fixing Isabella up with Phineas. Green-Eyed Monster: She is noticeably annoyed when Candace breaks her record of most badges earned in one day in "Fireside Girl Jamboree". Might be aVisual Punconsidering she actuallyhasgreen eyes.

characters.name: Holly
characters.description: Childish Tooth Gap: While not consistent, she's usually drawn with prominent front teeth with a visible gap between them. The Generic Girl: She's the most normal of the Fireside Girls all things considered and doesn't have many quriks. Girlish Pigtails: Holly has pigtails, which befit her being a young girl scout. Odd Friendship: "Happy Birthday, Isabella" has her talk to Candace about her busting habits. Sassy Black Woman: Downplayed. She's the sole regular African-American of the group and has her moments of snark from time to time.

characters.name: Katie
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: Katie is shown to be this several times. One example being her buzzing so she can "think like a bee". Cute Mute: She's usually silent, but she's also adorable and sweet hearted. Dumb Blonde: Downplayed, but she has her moments. Like herLiteral-Mindedconcept of "thinking like a bee" orforgetting to close the windowduring theZombie Apocalypse. The Friends Who Never Hang: Due to her beingThe Quiet One, she's spoken to Isabella the least and rarely stands next to her. Girlish Pigtails: Katie has pigtails, and she is a girl scout.

characters.name: Milly
characters.description: Bows for Cuteness: Milly, a Fireside Girl and aPerpetual Smiler, wears a yellow bow in her hair. Cannot Keep a Secret: As implied at the end of "Operation Crumb Cake" when Ferb tells Isabella that Milly blabbed to him about the letter to Phineas she didn't want him to know about.Isabella:Well, I guess we'll never know what was in that letter.Ferb:(smiling)No, I guess not. And neither will your "little crumb cake."Isabella:Milly!Milly:(does aNot-So-Innocent Whistle) Determinator: She states that she has one more "Help Thy Neighbor" patch from helping Phineas and Ferb than everyone else because she "went back one afternoon after everyone else went home." Fat and Skinny: Downplayed, but she's chubbier than the other girls. Innocent Blue Eyes: She's aPerpetual Smilergirl scout with blue eyes.

characters.name: Melissa
characters.description: A member of Lil' Sparks who makes an appearance in a Season 2 episode. As of Season 5, she graduates to the Fireside Girls. The Baby of the Bunch: After officially joining the Fireside Girls due to her being the youngest. The Bus Came Back: "Lord of the Firesides" is her first speaking role after her debut. Girlish Pigtails: Melissa wears blonde pigtails and is the youngest Fireside Girl. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: She's blonde and a very cute and sweet girl.

characters.name: Little Suzy Johnson
characters.description: Jeremy's little sister. Despite hercutesy demeanor, she's quite manipulative, and fiercely jealous of any girl trying to get Jeremy's attention. Beneath the Mask: Her actual personality is that of a psycho that threatens anyone who tries to take Jeremy from her, but this personality rarely manifests given how specific the situation is, and thus no one suspects it. Big Brother Attraction: Although it lacks any sexual qualities, she still wants Jeremy all to herself. And it's still very creepy. However, it's later implied that she doesn't really care that much about Jeremy and only likes the perks she gets from being his "favorite girl". Bitch in Sheep's Clothing:She pretends to be a dumb innocent girl, but in reality she is very smart, and cruel to whoever threatens her relationship with Jeremy. Child Prodigy: Far more knowledgeable and articulate than her age would suggest, though she hides this from most people.

characters.name: Nicolette Johnson
characters.description: Jeremy's cousin with an Australian accent. Fake Ultimate Hero: Candace hears her describing acts of derring-do and extreme sportsmanship she's committed. Jeremy informs Candace later that she was describing a video game she was playing. Foreign Fanservice: An attractive blonde with an Australian accent,wearing the same swimsuit as Candacebut filling it out better with her slender, feminine figure. Relative Error: Candace takes her for a romantic rival, only learning in the episode's resolution that she's Jeremy's cousin. Tomboy with a Girly Streak: A hardcoreGamer Chickbut very feminine in appearance.

characters.name: Eliza Fletcher
characters.description: Ferb's cousin and the step-cousin of Phineas and Candace. Hypocritical Humour: Eliza sings a song explaining to Candace all the things a fair lady should not do... while shifting into an aggressive punk rock tone that completely goes against what a fair lady should do. Meaningful Name: Her middle name is Beckham, which is also the surname of a well known English football (soccer) player, which also happens to be the main subject manner of the episode she appears in. It's also the surname of his wife, nicknamed "Posh" due to her image as theProper LadyofThe Spice Girls. Her first name is a reference toMy Fair Lady, as is the episode title, except that she's Professor Higgins to Candace's Eliza Doolittle. Nice Girl: She reluctantly but still willingly helps Candace act more 'ladylike' and is generally nice to both her and Jeremy. Proper Lady: Is what she's been raised up to be this from an early age.

characters.name: Monty Monogram
characters.description: Major Monogram's son who recently graduated from the High School Without A Cool Acronym, and now wants to fight evil like his father. The Ace: Displayed aNightwing-level combination of skilled acrobatics and combat skills in his debut appearance. Alliterative Name: Both his first and last name begin with a "M". Chekhov's Skill: Acrobatics. He mentions Major Monogram putting him in many classes growing up, and it's this skill that he uses to get the upper hand onRodrigo. Dating Catwoman: With Vanessa. Downplayed as she's not evil, and is just affiliated with her (kind of) evil father and doesn't approve of his lifestyle most of the time.

characters.name: Django Brown
characters.description: A friend of Phineas and Ferb's. His father is an installation artist, and some of his father's love of the arts seems to have rubbed off on him. Other than that, there's not much to say about him, which is probably why he's not seen much in later episodes. The Bus Came Back: Both he and Jenny finally have brief speaking roles again in the season four episode "The Inator Method". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Django was featured prominently in four early episodes, and was even a member of Phineas and Ferb's close-knit group of friends. After "Oil on Candace", he disappeared from the main cast and has been seen only in a handful of non-speaking cameos. A Day in the Limelight: "Oil on Candace" serves as his episode, where he tries to impress his dad by painting the Unpainted Desert. Demoted to Extra: Originally appeared in 2 episodes as one of the boys' friends, now generally absent.

characters.name: Jenny Brown
characters.description: A hippy-dippy friend of Candace's who shows up on occasion.Word of Godhassaidthat she is Django's sister. Like Django, she has suffered from beingOut of Focuson the show. Action Girl: Parodied in "Phineas and Ferb-Busters!", when Candace makes her and Stacy go through some physically taxing exercises so they can assist her in busting Phineas and Ferb. In a straighter example, she helps fight off the Norm Bot invasion in the first movie. The Bus Came Back: Both she and Django finally have brief speaking roles again in the Season 4 episode "The Inator Method". Demoted to Extra: After Season 1, Jenny rarely appears on the show outside of cameos. Flat Character: Besides her being aGranola Girl, we don't know anything more about her.

characters.name: Irving Du Bois
characters.description: A nerdy local kid who was introduced in "Hide and Seek" as an obsessive fan of Phineas and Ferb and their ambitious antics. He tags along with their daily projects on occasion in later episodes. When he's not geeking out over Phineas and Ferb, Irving can be seen butting heads with his equally geeky older brother Albert. Absurd Phobia: He fears, of all things, the color lavender. All There in the Script: His last name. Confirmed by Swampy Marsh on Twitter after not being mentioned in the show... yet. Ambiguously Bi: He's among Phineas and Ferb's biggest fans (and visibly sighs when Phineas mentions people "who love him right back") and also hits on Candace, Stacy, and the Fireside Girls (except for Isabellabarring an inator-related occasion). Annoying Younger Sibling: To his brother Albert; Albert finds Irving's fanboy behaviour annoying.

characters.name: Albert Du Bois
characters.description: Irving's older brother, with whom he often butts heads. All There in the Script: His last name isn't mentioned in the show. Big Brother Bully: Often mean to Irving, even physically abusing him at times. Expressive Mask: His glasses,Depending on the Artist. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: Downplayed. He wears glasses, and he's cold and rude to his brother.

characters.name: Coltrane
characters.description: A member of Jeremy's band and a love interest to Stacy. A Day in the Limelight: He has a relatively large role in "The Baljeatles", in which he's tutoring Baljeet at rock n' roll camp, begins dating Stacy, and his revamped character design debuts, all implying the intention of him becoming anAscended Extra. Later episodes, however, return him to an incidental role. The band is, after all, called Jeremy and the Incidentals (we still knownothingabout the drummer). Flat Character: We know that he's into music, but that's about it. Foil: In "The Baljeatles", his and Stacy's budding attraction serves as a foil to the far more insecure Candace's relationship with Jeremy. Ink-Suit Actor: In "The Baljeatles", he's given a new character design that more closely resembles his voice actor Corbin Bleu, with a darker skin tone and the iconic hairstyle Bleu wears in theHigh School Musicalseries. However, that design only appeared in one other episode before the rest of the original run reverted him back to his original design, with shorter hair and a hat, though the darker skin remained. The revival series returns him to the Bleu-like character design.

characters.name: Mandy, Thaddeus, and Thor
characters.description: Niece and nephews of the Flynn-Fletchers' next-door neighbor Mrs. Weaver. Always Someone Better: Learn this the hard way when Phineas and Ferb outclass them in their debut episode. They never challenge the titular duo again. Annoying Younger Sibling: Like Candace, Mandy considers her brothers' projects to be annoying. Unlike Phineas and Ferb, however, Thaddeus and Thor really areJerkasses. Bratty Half-Pint: Thaddeus and Thor are obnoxious young children who always put down other kids and try to one-up them. Break the Haughty: Thaddeus and Thor areveryquickly humbled upon seeing Phineas and Ferb's fort, to the point where Mandy claims the duo broke their brains. She later begrudgingly admits that Candace's brothers' inventions are better. It should be noted that shedoesuse an invention by Phineas and Ferb later in the series.

characters.name: Vanessa's Friends
characters.description: Amicable Exes: While Vanessa finds Johnny's dramatic personality annoying, and he doesn't take the breakup well at first, they do eventually agree to be friends after breaking up. The Fashionista: Lacie is shown to enjoy talking about fashion, and she compliments Birgitte's skirt in "Night of the Living Pharmacists". Genre Blindness: In "Night of the Living Pharmacists", Vanessa's gal pals casually suggest investigating noises, splitting up, and hiding, which are all foolish things to do in zombie stories. No Full Name Given: It's unknown what any of their last names are. Plot Allergy: "Skiddely Whiffers" reveals that Johnny and Lacie are allergic to bees.

characters.name: Marty the Rabbit Boy
characters.description: Bait-and-Switch Silhouette: Both times he appears, Candace mistakes his shadow for that of Phineas, and the shadow of his blender for that of Ferb, but then it turns out to just be Marty and the blender. Everything Is an Instrument: He uses his blender to play music. Funny Animal: He's a rabbit, but unlike Dennis, he's fully anthropomorphic and looks more like a human than a real bunny. Furry Reminder: He's a fully anthropomorphic rabbit, who exists alongside Dennis, aPartially Civilised Animalrabbit. No Full Name Given: We don't know his last name.

characters.name: Clyde and Betty Jo Flynn
characters.description: Linda's parents and Phineas' grandparents. They've got a bit of a mischievous streak in them, as seen in their introductory episode "Get That Bigfoot Outta My Face!" All Relatives Share a Surname: Phineas and Candace's maternal grandparents are named Clyde and Betty Jo Flynn despite being their mother Linda's parents and not theirdisappeared biological dadwhich hints their biological dad changed his name to Flynn or after Linda was either divorced or widowed, she changed her name back to Flynn and then Flynn-Fletcher via marrying Lawrence Fletcher. Cool Old Guy: They're more than happy to have their grandkids—and all their friends up to stay at the lake house, which they operate as a summer camp, complete with a fake, but very convincing bigfoot. Happily Married: Clyde and Betty Jo are quite affectionate and seem very happily married. Hidden Depths: Part 1 of "Where's Perry?" shows that Clyde has a book on monotreme manners.Betty Jo:You have a book on monotreme manners?Clyde:You don't know everything about me.

characters.name: Reginald and Winifred Fletcher
characters.description: Lawrence's thoroughly British parents and Ferb's grandparents. Reginald was a bit of a thrill-seeker in his youth, and performed as a stunt motorcyclist known as "The Flying Fishmonger". Bookworm: Winifred is hinted to be this in "Elementary Dear Stacy" due to her vast collection of Sherlock Holmes books. Cool Old Guy: Reginald likes to skateboard, fly a biplane, and he's still perfectly capable of motorcycle jumping over gorges. High-Class Glass: Reginald wears a monocle, fitting for a proper old British gent. Retired Badass: Reginald used to do daredevil stunts as The Flying Fishmonger. He briefly takes up the mantle again with Phineas and Ferb in "The Flying Fishmonger".

characters.name: Roger Doofenshmirtz
characters.description: Danville's mayor and Dr. Doofenshmirtz's "goody two-shoes" younger brother. A frequent target of Heinz's animosity, for being the favored son by their mother and generally out-performing him at everything when the two were growing up. The Ahnold: He's got the chiseled body of a typical action star, but he shares his brother's pointy nose. Big Little Brother: He is definitely more mature and more physically impressive thanHeinz, though he is in fact the younger sibling. Innocently Insensitive: In many of Heinz's backstories, Roger makes his brother's life worse not through malice, but through genuine obliviousness to the suffering their parents put him through. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He's a mild example of aSleazy Politician, but he's helped others and is hinted to be why Danville is a great place to live; he even spent twenty years trying to restore Heinz's painting.

characters.name: Charlene Doofenshmirtz
characters.description: Dr. Doofenshmirtz's ex-wife. Not much is known about her, other than she's rich and that she and Heinz get along pretty well, despite some back-and-forth snark. Despite her daughter's insistence,she doesn't believe that her ex is an evil scientist. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She's a dark-haired decently pretty woman who's quite aloof towards her ex Doof.Like Mother, Like Daughter, after all. Amicable Exes: She snarks at Heinz occasionally regarding his odd money spending habits and his ineptitude at building things when they were together, but she is genuinely friendly with him most of the time, most evident in her near-constant attempts to get Vanessa to warm up to him. Apparently their marriage ended because they "both wanted different things" (and also because she apparently hated Heinz's puppet Mister Tomato). Notably, Heinz hasneverattempted to screw her over throughout all his schemes and remains civil with her. She even kept the Doofenshmirtz name and shows up to family reunions. However,Vendpocalypsepaints a different picture, and their divorce wasn’t exactly as amicable as we were led to believe. Deadpan Snarker: She often responds to the craziness happening around Doof with subdued sarcasm, and sometimes does so to Vanessa as well when she tries to talk about what Doof is getting up to. Failed a Spot Check: She is oblivious to the fact that her ex-husband is an evil scientist, and yet, somehow, fails to notice the big sign on the side of Doof's building that clearly says "DoofenshmirtzEVILInc."

characters.name: Doofenshmirtz's Parents
characters.description: The unnamed parents of Heinz and Roger and the culprits of the former'sHilariously Abusive Childhood. Abusive Parents: Exaggerated andPlayed for Laughs. Their neglect and mistreatment of Heinzstartswith both of themsomehow not being present for the day of his birth.They've forced him to be a lawn gnome, shamed him for being too afraid to jump from a several story high diving board, and made him throw his own birthday parties when he was six years old. At one point, Heinz was disowned and raised by ocelots. But the sheer number of traumatic events in his life coupled with the sheer ridiculousness of them causes their treatment of him to veer intoHilariously Abusive Childhood. Ambiguous Situation:It's never exactly statedwhythey hated Heinz so much, just that they do. A part of their abuse could be cultural since their neighbor forced his son to be a lawn ornament, too, (specifically a lawn jockey) but the rest of their mistreatment just seems to be them being callousJerkasseswho don't care about and/or respect their sons unless they "earn" it from them, such as favoring Roger for being successful and good at kickball, as opposed toHeinzwho is frequently stated to be unlucky and unsuccessful.Mrs. Doofenshmirtz seems to live in the same town as her sons, while Mr. Doofenshmirtz lives back in their home country. It is possible that they are divorced, although this is never stated onscreen. It's never exactly statedwhythey hated Heinz so much, just that they do. A part of their abuse could be cultural since their neighbor forced his son to be a lawn ornament, too, (specifically a lawn jockey) but the rest of their mistreatment just seems to be them being callousJerkasseswho don't care about and/or respect their sons unless they "earn" it from them, such as favoring Roger for being successful and good at kickball, as opposed toHeinzwho is frequently stated to be unlucky and unsuccessful. Mrs. Doofenshmirtz seems to live in the same town as her sons, while Mr. Doofenshmirt

characters.name: Lyla Lolliberry
characters.description: An agent of C.O.W.C.A. (short forCanadianOrganizationWithoutACoolAcronym) who teams up with Perry in order to stop a joined plot between Doofenshmirtz and Lila's arch-nemesis, Professor Bannister. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: Lyla, being Canadian and unfamiliar with Doof's schemes, tells Perry to get that "inator", putting emphasis on the first syllable, and Doof says, "It's pronounced 'inator'!" Alliterative Name:LylaLolliberry. She describes her family as alliterative, suggesting the other Lolliberries also have given names that start with "L". Courteous Canadian: It doesn't stop her from being a totalAction Girl, but her sense of politesse being Canadian has a tendency of slowing her down, with her lamenting the fact that Doofenshmirtz left the toilet seat up and putting the hazard lights onbeforeevacuating everyone from the runaway train. Fair Cop: She has a pretty design and one moment where her jacket gets pulled off during a fight. She's notably one of the few human members of O.W.C.A. overall.

characters.name: Aloyse "Rodney" von Roddenstein
characters.description: Another mad scientist and rival within L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N. to Doofenshmirtz. Bald of Evil: Evil and prominently bald. Characterization Marches On: During his previous appearances, he was shown to be as goofy as Doofenshmirtz, that is until "Save Summer", where he becomes completely psychopathic in nature by revealing his ruthless plan to bring in a new Ice Age that would endanger the entire world population, an act that everyone (including Doofenshmirtz) finds to be very disturbing. Even Perry thinks of Rodney to be far more despicable than Doofenshmirtz as the imminent cataclysm wouldendanger his host familyas well. Creator Cameo: Voiced by one of the writers on the show. Diabolical Mastermind: Upon hearing of Doofenshmirtz's successful scheme of moving the Earth to an early autumn, Rodney takes the opportunity to exploit the event, effectively becoming the brains behind L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N.'s plot to rule the Earth. He arranged his fellow villains to capture nearly all of O.W.C.A.'s agents, hold the world for ransom, and contact the world leaders to meet their demands by any means.

characters.name: Dr. Diminutive
characters.description: An unhinged evil scientist with a chip on his shoulder over his short size. Butt-Monkey: He gets his ass handed to him on "Let's All Dance Until We're Sick", gets kicked out of the L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N. pageant for his short stature, and gets thrown in jail after steali-borrowingDoof's inator. It's Probably Nothing: He often dismisses strange noises as the building settling. The Napoleon: If he had it his way, the trope would be named "The Dr. Diminutive". See his quote above. Thing-O-Matic: He calls his inventions "-erators".

characters.name: Professor Bannister
characters.description: Lyla Lolliberry's arch-nemesis. An evil scientist from Canada (later revealed to actually be from Greenland) who plots to annex the former into the latter to reinvigorate Greenland's low national pride. Cloudcuckoolander: His plan to annex Canada into Greenland involves stealing its symbol of national pride (Precious Albert the Moose) in order to demoralize Canadians of their heritage and raise up Greenlandic national pride.Doofenshmirtz considers his plan to be both idiotic and unnecessarily complicated, even by his standards. Fauxreigner: Was assumed by both C.O.W.C.A. and L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N. to be from Canada, until he reveals himself to actually be from Greenland. Doofenshmirtz claims to him that misrepresenting your country of origin to the L.O.V.E.M.U.F.F.I.N. organization is a serious offense,but doesn't go into detail as to what exactly the punishment is. Non-Action Guy: Prefers to let his robots do the fighting for him. Patriotic Fervor: Is very fond of his home country of Greenland, and will do anything to bring it further glory.

characters.name: Esmeralda Poofenplotz
characters.description: Yet another mad scientist, the nemesis of Isabella's pet chihuahua Pinky. Alliterative Name: Though not so when her first name, Esmeralda, is included. Catchphrase: Has one whenever her plans get foiled by Pinky, similar to Doofenshmirtz's.Poofenplotz:Curse you, Pinky the Chihuahua! Cloudcuckoolander: She thinks eating royal jelly will make her the queen of the world... and give her a large abdomen for laying eggs, but she claims she can live with that. She soon learns the hard way after realizing that her hypothesis is faulty. Distaff Counterpart: Dr. Doofenshmirtz, but an even less competent one according to Doofenshmirtz himself.

characters.name: Professor Mystery
characters.description: Peter the Panda's actual nemesis from Seattle. Technically only seen in a glimpse into an alternate universe. Does This Remind You of Anything?: As with all Peter the Panda episodes, the relationship between an Agent and Evil Scientist is portrayed like a real-like relationship between a couple. In this case, Mystery is "theotherEvil Scientist" in Heinz and Peter's "affair". Flat Character: At least from Peter's point of view. His focus on being mysterious leads to Peter finding him as a lot less interesting than, say, Doofenshmirtz. Freudian Excuse: After Heinz gets him to talk to Peter, admits a lot of his villainy is based in his parents abandoning him as a child.Phineas and Ferb's plot in the episode frees them from their locked capsule and they reunite. Generic Doomsday Villain: Considered to be oneIn-Universe. Peter the Panda eventually gets fed up of dealing with him because it's all work, no mystique, and Doofenshmitz puts it into song:Dr. Doofenshmirtz:You can can it with the mystery,you don't have to be so vague! (So vague!)Give your nemesis some history,all the reasons you're a rotten egg!

characters.name: Love Händel
characters.description: A former hair metal band from the early nineties. They were a favorite of Linda and Lawrence until they split up. As an anniversary gift to their parents, Phineas and Ferb spend the episode "Dude, We're Getting the Band Back Together!" trying to convince them to get together for a reunion concert. Adults Are Useless: The only adults inAcross the 2nd Dimensionto (somewhat) avert this. More so in a deleted scene where Danny gets to take out at least one Normbot with a simpleOffhand Backhand! All Drummers Are Animals: Subverted with Sherman. He looked just as wild as the others in the band's heyday, but went on to work in a library and is by far their most laid-back member. While the others go back to their old costumes after the reunion, Sherman in nearly all of his appearances retains his plain, boring librarian outfit, mainly because he grew aBalloon Bellyand can no longer fit in it. Appeal to Flattery: How the boys convince Bobbi to reunite with the other band members; by telling him that he's the one who steals the show. Autobots, Rock Out!: Their main role during theFinal BattleinAcross the 2nd Dimensionis to provide live musical accompaniment.

characters.name: Farmer and His Wife
characters.description: A farmer and his nagging wife who are always down on their luck, until what the wife says ends up falling to them from the sky exactly on cue. They reappear as aRunning GaginHamster & Gretel. Arbitrary Skepticism: The wife always seems to think the farmer is being lazy by waiting for something he needs to fall out of the sky, even though it happens to them every time. Bait-and-Switch: After the Farmer starts a sheep farm without any sheep, his wife chides him for not having any sheep, but the Farmer assures her that he ordered some... and then a huge bundle of sheep rolls by. The Farmer then notes those aren't the sheep he ordered; they're actually getting delivered that afternoon, meaning he thought ahead for once. Born Lucky: As incompetent as the farmer is, he always gets exactly what he needs at the most opportune of times through sheer luck alone. Cue the Flying Pigs: The wife incredulously asks the farmer if he thinks what he needs will fall out of the sky, and it always does immediately after, oftentimes landing right on top of her.

characters.name: Vivian Garcia-Shapiro
characters.description: Isabella's Jewish-Mexican mother and Linda's friend. Affectionate Nickname: She calls Isabella "Isa". Foreign Queasine: She often makes Jewish-Mexican delicacies such as Matzo-Ball-ritos and Kreplach Tortillas. Gratuitous Spanish: She sprinkles some Spanish into her dialogue. Housewife: She is not seen working, except as the bassist for Linda's jazz trio. It is not until "Act Your Age" that it is revealed she owns a Mexican-Jewish restaurant called "Nosh Olé".

characters.name: Mrs. Johnson
characters.description: Jeremy and Little Suzy's mother and another friend of Linda's. Flat Character: She has barely any distinguishing characteristics, other than her support of wildlife. No Name Given: She is only referred to as "Mrs. Johnson", and the only thing close to a name is that she refers to herself as "Hawkeye Johnson". Soapbox Sadie: She is a supporter of wildlife conservation. Suddenly Speaking: She was first only seen as a background character and as the drummer for Linda's jazz trio. It wasn't until the third season that she was given lines.

characters.name: Dink Winkerson
characters.description: The disturbingly UV-sensitive host ofDanville Today, also an escaped convict. Ascended Extra: In the original run of the series, he only appeared in two episodes, "It's a Mud, Mud, Mud, Mud World" and "For Your Ice Only", where his only gag was being overshadowed by Isabella's deep masculine voice. His role as news anchor was mainly replaced by either Bridgette Oshinomi or Gordon Gutsofanemu. In season 5, he has a more dominant presence. Cardboard Prison: He has apparently escaped from prison so many times that he has lost count. Kent Brockman News: He usually serves as the exposition for the episode, or sometimes as a sportscaster.

characters.name: Norm
characters.description: A slightly scatterbrained android build by Dr. Doofenshmirtz to destroy Perry the Platypus in the episode "Greece Lightning", based on the Doctormisinterpreting an old film stripabout how"the greatest enemy of the platypus is man". Norm eventually started showing up in later episodes helping out Doofenshmirtz with the occasional evil scheme. He has some of the personality attributes of an eerily-cheerful office-worker fromThe '50s, with an occasional sarcastic streak. Affably Evil: He's fond of spouting random dialogue more appropriate to a married, white-collar suburbanite than a killer robot originally designed to attack platypi on sight. Anti-Villain: Every time he has served as an antagonist, he is either following orders or believes he canearn Doofenshmirtz's affectionby doing so. Artificial Stupidity: Early on, he was very clueless and didn't understand how to play hide and seek. Ascended Extra: Started out as one of Doof's inventions (after learning "the enemy of the platypus is man", hebuilt a robot man), and then began making more appearances as Doof's lovable but bungling henchman, and even had a few episodes centered around him.

characters.name: Balloony
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: This was ambiguous in his first appearance, but "Meapless in Seattle" appears to confirm that he does have a mind of his own. Balloon of Doom: Chooses Mitch over Doofenshmirtz. Companion Cube: A balloon that Doofenshmirtz considered to be his best childhood friend, though he is at least implied to be sentient. Insistent Terminology: Mitch insists that Balloony's name is really "Colin". That "Heinz" signature on him? That's just a birthmark. Non-Standard Character Design: It's just a balloon with a face... a disturbingly realistically-rendered face.

characters.name: Dennis the Rogue Rabbit
characters.description: Badass Adorable: A super-criminal bunny rabbit. Beneath the Mask: Initially appearing to be a calm and arrogant rival, he reveals his true nature as a criminal who is one of Perry's most challenging opponents. Evil Counterpart: More or less what Perry would be if he ever went over to the dark side. Fallen Hero: A former O.W.C.A. agent. Hair-Raising Hare: A cute bunny and one of the most dangerous villains in the series.

characters.name: Pinky the Chihuahua
characters.description: Isabella's pet chihuahua, later revealed to be an O.W.C.A. secret agent. He works in a different division from Perry the Platypus, under Admiral Acronym, and is the nemesis of Professor Poofenplotz. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Like all O.W.C.A. agents, he wears a hat. Action Pet: A secret agent of O.W.C.A.. Badass Adorable: A secret agent chihuahua. Character Tics: Being a chihuahua, he constantly has the jitters and is rarely seen not shivering. Despite this, he has incredible self-control.

characters.name: Terry the Turtle
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Like all O.W.C.A. agents, he wears a hat. Action Pet: A secret agent of O.W.C.A.. Animal Superheroes: This is the central conceit of the O.W.CA, that all their agents are animals. Anthropomorphic Zig-Zag: Presumably. He's never seen outside of agent mode. Canon Immigrant: Originally made for the Across the Second Dimension video game forWiiandPlayStation 3, but Dan and Swampy liked him so much he's got counterparts in the first and second dimensions.

characters.name: Planty the Potted Plant
characters.description: Animate Plant: He looks like a potted plant, and he doesn't talk, but if his reaction to being relocated in "Just Our Luck" means anything, it means he's sapient. The Cameo:Blink and you'll miss it, but he appears inThe OWCA Files. Companion Cube: He's a potted plant, but Doofenshmirtz and Major Monogram treat him as if he was as sapient as any animal agent.And they might be right to do so. Fedora of Asskicking: Just like any other O.W.C.A. agent, he wears a fedora. Full-Name Basis: Even Major Monogram, who normally only uses agents' codenames, calls him "Planty the Potted Plant". Most likely since Perry is already "Agent P".

characters.name: Harry the Hyena, Karen the Cat, and Maggie the Macaw
characters.description: New agents of O.W.C.A. being trained by Perry alongside another recruit, Heinz Doofenshmirtz the "Ocelot". Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Being O.W.C.A. agents, they all wear hats. Amazing Technicolor Population: Harry is a purple hyena, though he didn't have that in his first appearance way back in "Toy to the World" Big Eater: Harry is seen eating an armful of burgers in a freezeframe of Perry's squad working at a burger joint, and in another freezeframe is competing in a hot dog eating contest. The Big Guy: Harry isn't just the muscle of the squad, he's also the biggest member of Perry's squad, not counting Doofenshmirtz.

characters.name: Peter the Panda
characters.description: A secret agent panda from Seattle who temporarily replaced Perry as Doofenshmirtz's nemesis. It was later revealed that this replacement was actually part of Doofenshmirtz's plan to defeat the O.W.C.A., upon which Peter and Perry worked together to foil the scheme. Peter has since shown up to assist Perry on several other missions. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Like all O.W.C.A. agents, he wears a hat. Alliterative Name:Peter thePanda Animal Superheroes: A secret agent panda. Animals Not to Scale: He is much smaller than a real giant panda.

characters.name: Meap
characters.description: A small, adorable alien who initially crash landed in Phineas and Ferb's yard and was nicknamed "Meap" based on his curious vocalizations. In spite of his appearance he is strong enough to defeat opponents many times his size and turns out to be an intergalactic security agent in charge of stopping Mitch. It has been shown that he belongs to a species whose language is composed solely of the word "Meap" and can shoot destructive rainbow-colored beams from their mouth. Aliens Speaking English: Downplayed. He can be heard speaking English, but only if he wears a translator. Badass Adorable: In spite of his appearance, he is an experienced member of theSpace Policefor good reason. Borrowed Catchphrase: Before the character was introduced, Candace had a tendency to say, "Meap..." as a form of surprise, such as in "The Fast and the Phineas", "It's a Mud, Mud, Mud, Mud World", "Backyard Aquarium" and "Candace Disconnected". Breath Weapon: He can fire a destructive beam from his mouth.

characters.name: Mitch
characters.description: An evil alien poacher who cruises the galaxies looking for rare specimens and occasionally tries to take over his home planet. An Alien Named "Bob": An alien named Mitch. Aliens Speaking English: Downplayed - he speaks English, but only if he wears a translator. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: Does not like to be called a zookeeper, as it "legitimizes" his evildoing. Beware the Silly Ones: Very silly and hammy, but he's still a serious threat and comes close to winning in "Meapless in Seattle".

characters.name: Super Super Big Doctor
characters.description: The main antagonist ofPhineas and Ferb The Movie: Candace Against the Universe. First introduced as the leader of Feebla-Oot, and is first portrayed as friendly to Candace, but is then revealed to be a ruthless dictator who enslaves a planet's inhabitants with her mind control plant. Bait-and-Switch Comment: Super Super Big Doctor did this twice to get away to prevent her plans from being interfered by Phineas, Ferb, and the whole gang. Big Bad: At first, she seems friendly, but is later revealed to be the main villain. Big Sister Bully: Super Super Big Doctor had her younger brothers locked in the dungeon just because everyone thought they were more special than she was. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Super Super Big Doctor comes off as someone who relates to what Candace is going through with her brothers, stating that she used to be the same way. However, it is revealed that she is apetty, childishoverlord who enslaved the planet and only wanted Candace so she could restore her brainwashing plant to life.

characters.name: Talking Zebra
characters.description: A mysterious talking zebra who tends to show up whenever Candace is hallucinating or dreaming. He seems to think Candace's name is "Kevin". Accidental Misnaming: He thinks Candace's name is Kevin. The Bus Came Back: He didn't make a lot of appearances after "Monster from the Id". But he made his triumphant return in "Dry Another Day" to inform "Kevin" that the giant ice luge she saw was not a hallucination. Feather Fingers: He has inexplicably prehensile hooves. Identical Stranger: This trope is why he calls Candace "Kevin". Kevin is an important political figure in his world, who happens to look a lot like Candace, and might even be that world's version of Candace under a different name.

characters.name: Klimpaloon, the magical old-timey bathing suit that lives in the Himalayas
characters.description: A magical old-timey bathing suit that lives in the Himalayas. Insistent Terminology: He is seldom referred to as simply "Klimpaloon"; it's usually theentireepithet of "Klimpaloon,the magical old-timey bathing suitthatlives in the Himalayas". Living Clothes: Even his loose threads are capable of movement and thought. Old-Timey Bathing Suit: He is a living, old-fashioned swimsuit. The Unintelligible: All he says is "Nang nang nang nang nang."

characters.name: Giant Floating Baby Head
characters.description: The inexplicable oversized infant head that defies gravity. Nobody understands why it exists or where it comes from. Ambiguous Gender: Its gender, if it has one, is unknown. Another Dimension: Seems to come from one, seeing as one of the other dimensions seen inAcross the Second Dimensionis full of them. Early-Installment Weirdness: In "It's a Mud, Mud, Mud, Mud World", it does not seem to be sentient (aside from the sound of a goo) at all and is just a prop. Its second appearance, "The Monster of Phineas-and-Ferbenstein", it is a living monster, but doesn't float. Flying Face: It's a giant baby head that floats.

characters.name: The Bug Trio
characters.description: A trio of bugs consisting of the intelligent leader Napoleon and his dimwitted subordinates Wendell and Floyd, who want to make contact with humans. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Napoleon wears a sash. Butt-Monkey: They never succeed at anything, and are subject to all sorts of injuries along the way. The Ditz: Floyd, and to a lesser extent Wendell are probably the only characters to properly avert the show's "no idiots" policy.Napoleon:Okay, where's Floyd? Floyd!(Floyd walks onscreen)Floyd:Sorry, sir, ran into a spider web, lost my wings.Napoleon:They're behind you, Floyd.Floyd:(looks behind himself and sees his wings)I found them, sir.Napoleon:So, as I was saying-Floyd:They were behind me.Napoleon:Yes, we've established that. Four-Legged Insect: They are only shown with four limbs.

characters.name: Beatrice the Candace Suit
characters.description: Heel–Face Turn:She eventually agrees to stop forcing other people to wear her and ends up turning to the side of good and dating Klimpaloon. Living Clothes: She's a sentient bodysuit. People Puppets: She can control people's bodies by making them wear her. Special Person, Normal Name: A sentient bodysuit namedBeatrice.

characters.name: PhineasFlynn-2
characters.description: Phineas' counterpart from the second dimension. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Subverted at first, thenplayed straight. Badass Bookworm:After joining the Resistance. Child Prodigy: After being inspired by first dimension Phineas and Ferb, he turns out to be as brilliant as they are. Deep Cover Agent:Though not at first.

characters.name: FerbFletcher-2
characters.description: Ferb's counterpart from the second dimension. Alliterative Name:FerbFletcher. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome:Subverted at first, then played straight. Badass Bookworm:After joining the Resistance. Child Prodigy: After being inspired by first dimension Phineas and Ferb, he turns out to be as brilliant as they are.

characters.name: CandaceFlynn-2
characters.description: Candace's counterpart from the second dimension. Action Girl: One only needs to see Candace-2'sfirst encounter with the Norm-botsfor proof. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Shows off what Candace can do when her busting instincts are turned on someone who actuallydeservesit. Arch-Enemy: To Doof-2 and his family, as they took over their Tri-State Area. Asskicking Leads to Leadership: The leader of the Resistance and easily one of the biggest badasses in the entire series. Everything she does is a moment of awesome, but especially saving the first dimension characters by pushing a giant lawn gnome off of a ledge, jumping on it as it falls, and using a pair of grappling hooks to turn it into a robot wrecking ball.

characters.name: IsabellaGarcia-Shaprio-2
characters.description: Isabella's counterpart from the second dimension. Action Girl: Technically she doesn't get in on much action in the movie, but she appears to be this based on her general personality and rank in the Resistance. She does get more time to shine in "Tales of the Resistance". Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Fights in the Resistance as second in command. Badass Adorable: Helps Candace-2 take down some giant robotic ants in "Tales of the Resistance", and is shown to have some mad dodging skills while facing the animal cyborgs. Catchphrase: "Whatcha doin'?" She tends to use a far more serious tone than Isabella-1 when saying it.

characters.name: BaljeetTjinder-2
characters.description: Baljeet's counterpart from the second dimension. Adorably Precocious Child: Insists on being addressed as "Dr. Baljeet". All There in the Script: His last name is never mentioned, but is presumably Tjinder like his first dimension counterpart, first confirmed by Swampy Marsh on Twitter. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Without Phineas and Ferb aroundto make him mostly redundant, Alternate Baljeet quite effectively serves the role as the brains of the Resistance. Bollywood Nerd: Indian and nerdy.

characters.name: Buford VanStomm-2
characters.description: Buford's counterpart from the second dimension. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Fights in the Resistance. Amazon Chaser: Apparently has a crush on Candace-2. The Big Guy: Brash and physically oriented. Creator Cameo: Voiced by one of the writers on the show.

characters.name: HeinzDoofenshmirtz-2
characters.description: Dr. Doofenshmirtz's counterpart from the second dimension. Amicable Exes: Subverted...because he and Charlene-2 were never divorced at all. Arch-Enemy: To Candace-2. The Bad Guy Wins: He managed to take over his Tri-State Area and ruled it with an iron fist for 5 years. Subverted in the film ending, where his plot to invade the original Tri-State Area is foiled, leading to his arrest, though he would later escape (with the help of his family) 2 months later. Beard of Evil: Unlike Doofenshmirtz-1, he is evidently capable of growing facial hair.

characters.name: Perry the Platyborg
characters.description: Perry's counterpart from the second dimension. Action Pet: A secret agent before and after Doofenshmirtz-2's reign. Alliterative Name: Perry the Platyborg. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: A teal platypus. Amplified Animal Aptitude

characters.name: FrancisMonogram-2
characters.description: Major Monogram's counterpart from the second dimension. Big Ol' Unibrow: Like Monogram-1. Creator Cameo: Voiced by one of the creators of the show. Deep Cover Agent:Judging by the fact that he appears to be acquainted with the Resistance. The Dog Bites Back:This "indentured executive assistant" is the one who leads the arrest of Doof-2 at the end.Monogram-2: Book him, ladies.

characters.name: The Firestorm Girls
characters.description: A squad of resistance fighters that aid Candace-2, and the second dimension counterparts of the Fireside Girls. Action Girls: As members of the Resistance. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Fight in the Resistance. Badass Adorable: All of them just like their counterparts from the first dimension. Deep Cover Agents: As members of the Resistance.

characters.name: Norm Bots
characters.description: 2D Visuals, 3D Effects: They're rendered in 3D. Cloudcuckoolander: This is one of their two modes. In this mode, they play it even more so than Norm-1. Dirty Cop: Assigned to keep the entire Tri-State Area in check under Doof-2's orders, including the local streets. Energy Weapon: Can shoot these from their arm cannons. Evil Counterpart: To Norm-1, but more menacing and strong in numbers.

characters.name: CharleneDoofenshmirtz-2
characters.description: Charlene's counterpart from the second dimension. Action Mom: Vanessa-2's motherand much more proficient in battle than Doof-2. Amicable Exes: Subverted...because she and Doof-2 were never divorced at all. The Bad Guy Wins: She managed to free her husband from prison and escape with him (and their daughter) to evade arrest. Big Bad: Of the episode sequel.

characters.name: VanessaDoofenshmirtz-2
characters.description: Vanessa's counterpart from the second dimension. The Bad Guy Wins: She managed to help her parents evade arrest by having her boyfriend to drive them away in a hovercraft. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Not as much in-universe, as she revealed herself to be evil as her parents. Chekhov's Gunman: Even counting her deleted scene in the movie, she only appears in a couple of short segments with little relevance to the main plot.Until her final scene, in which she saves her parents from arrest, leaving the Second Dimension story arc on aSequel Hook. Daddy's Little Villain: Like her first dimension counterpart, she subverts this in that she appears to have little interest in doing evil directly...but also like her first dimension counterpart, she is willing to help her criminal parents escape arrest when they are captured.
